items.title: The expression-position whitespace rule: a spaced `<` after a name never opens a generic list (`a < b > (c)` reads as two comparisons, `List <i32>::new()` refused with the tight spelling) — B571 Q3's separable half, RULED "later, as its own item"
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-10 (lang-b-49's find, Order 49; placeholder id)
items.body: B571 S1 built the whitespace rule for ASCRIBED types only (RULED). In expression position a spaced `<` after a name still opens a generic list when one parses (`List <i32>::new()`, the paper's a05; `a < b > (c)` as the generic call `a<b>(c)`, a15). E284 (built beside this) gives that last reading a message naming both readings. The rule here would remove the reading: one rule for the language, the formatter already writes every generic list tight and every comparison spaced, the estate has 0 spaced generic lists (§5.2). Needs a census of unformatted sources first, then the parser change in `parse_chain_head`'s generic-head and `parse_member_call`'s fused-call generics, the spaced-list refusal reused (`ParseErrorReason::SpacedAscribedGenerics`, generalized), and E284's message retired. Sizing S.

items.title: Natively, `.filter(\|length\| *length > 1)` over a `List<usize>` dereferences the by-value closure parameter (`(*length) > 1usize`): rustc refuses E0614, JS prints the count
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-10 (lang-b-49's find, Order 49; placeholder id)
items.body: `["a", "bb", "ccc"].map(|word| word.len()).filter(|length| *length > 1).len()` builds on JS (prints 2) and is refused by rustc natively: the closure parameter is emitted `move |mut length: usize|` while the body keeps the source's `*length`. `filter`'s predicate takes `&T` (a view of a scalar element), the native emitter passes the element by value, and the explicit dereference survives. Either the parameter is emitted as `&usize` or the `*` on a scalar view read is dropped (transparent references R4). Found while pinning B571's native rows (the probe uses `length > 1` instead). Sizing S.

items.title: A `dyn` value at an annotated `let` of its concrete type is refused TWICE with the same narrowing message (`let square: Square = shape;`)
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-10 (lang-b-49's find, Order 49; placeholder id)
items.body: `let shape: dyn Shape = Square { side = 2 }; let square: Square = shape;` reports "Expected Square, but got dyn Shape instead: an object does not narrow back to the type it erased ..." twice at one span (B5: one diagnostic per mistake). An ascription `shape as Square` inherits it (B571 S2's downcast refusal is that message). Likely the readiness probe and the directed ask both report. Sizing XS.

items.title: `auto-annotations.md` §5's third naming tier (`std::reactive::Derive`, the full path) cannot be written: a type path in vilan resolves only through an IMPORTED module name, so `--fix` declines where the paper expected it to qualify — should type position admit absolute `std::`/`pkg::` paths?
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-10 (lang-b-49's find, Order 49; placeholder id)
items.body: B570 S1 built §5 as ruled (Q7: qualify, never import): a name in scope, else through an imported module (`reactive::Derive`, one child module deep). The full-path tier is refused by resolution ("`std` is a namespace, not a value; import the module first"), so a type the file reaches neither way is DECLINED with the import that would let it (`import std::fetch::ChunkResult;`). On kolt's tip that is 1 of 98 candidates (`shared.vl::hash` returns `Hash`). Options: (a) keep declining (built); (b) admit absolute `std::…`/`pkg::…` paths in type position, which would let `--fix` qualify every case without touching imports. Rec: (a) until a second case appears; the decline names the import. Sizing S for (b).
